title: I have to ...
summary: **have to** — «нужно, приходится, обязан»: когда обстоятельства или правила заставляют что-то делать. Есть настоящее (have/has to) и прошедшее (had to).
ru:
## Что значит have to
**have to + глагол** — «нужно, приходится, должен». Так мы говорим, когда что-то необходимо из-за обстоятельств, правил или расписания.
> I have to get up at six. — Мне нужно вставать в шесть.
> Jill has to work on Saturdays. — Джилл приходится работать по субботам.
> You have to wear a uniform at school. — В школе нужно носить форму.

## Настоящее: have to / has to
- I / we / you / they → **have to**
- he / she / it → **has to**
> We have to wait here. — Нам нужно ждать здесь.
> My brother has to study a lot. — Моему брату приходится много учиться.

## Прошлое: had to
> I had to walk home yesterday. — Вчера мне пришлось идти домой пешком.
> She had to leave early. — Ей пришлось уйти пораньше.
Одна форма для всех лиц.

## Вопросы и отрицания: do / does / did
В вопросах и отрицаниях добавляем вспомогательный глагол.
> Do you have to work today? — Тебе нужно сегодня работать?
> Does Tom have to wear a suit? — Тому нужно носить костюм?
> Why did they have to leave? — Почему им пришлось уйти?
> I don't have to get up early. — Мне не нужно рано вставать.
> She doesn't have to pay. — Ей не нужно платить.
> We didn't have to wait. — Нам не пришлось ждать.

## don't have to и mustn't — разные вещи!
> You **don't have to** come. — Ты не обязан приходить. (можно прийти, можно нет)
> You **mustn't** come. — Тебе нельзя приходить. (запрет)

## Типичные ошибки
- ~~He have to go.~~ → He **has to** go.
- ~~Do you have to went?~~ → Do you have to **go**?
- ~~I didn't had to work.~~ → I didn't **have to** work.
- ~~Does she has to work?~~ → Does she **have to** work?
- ~~I haven't to go.~~ → I **don't have to** go.
en:
## What does have to mean?
We use **have to + verb** when it is necessary to do something because of rules, a situation or a timetable.
> I have to get up at six.
> Jill has to work on Saturdays.
> You have to wear a uniform at school.

## Present: have to / has to
- I / we / you / they → **have to**
- he / she / it → **has to**
> We have to wait here.
> My brother has to study a lot.

## Past: had to
> I had to walk home yesterday.
> She had to leave early.
The form is the same for all persons.

## Questions and negatives: do / does / did
> Do you have to work today?
> Does Tom have to wear a suit?
> Why did they have to leave?
> I don't have to get up early.
> She doesn't have to pay.
> We didn't have to wait.

## don't have to and mustn't are different
> You **don't have to** come. (it is not necessary)
> You **mustn't** come. (it is forbidden)

## Common mistakes
- ~~He have to go.~~ → He **has to** go.
- ~~I didn't had to work.~~ → I didn't **have to** work.
- ~~Does she has to work?~~ → Does she **have to** work?
- ~~I haven't to go.~~ → I **don't have to** go.
structure:
## Утверждение
| Время | Подлежащее | Форма |
|---|---|---|
| Настоящее | I / we / you / they | have to + глагол |
| Настоящее | he / she / it | has to + глагол |
| Прошедшее | все лица | had to + глагол |

## Вопрос
| Время | Форма | Пример |
|---|---|---|
| Настоящее | Do + I/we/you/they + have to ...? | Do you have to go? |
| Настоящее | Does + he/she/it + have to ...? | Does he have to go? |
| Прошедшее | Did + подлежащее + have to ...? | Did she have to go? |

## Отрицание
| Время | Форма | Пример |
|---|---|---|
| Настоящее | don't / doesn't + have to | I don't have to wait. |
| Прошедшее | didn't + have to | We didn't have to pay. |

## Краткие ответы
> Do you have to work? — Yes, I do. / No, I don't.
> Does he have to go? — Yes, he does. / No, he doesn't.
> Did you have to wait? — Yes, I did. / No, I didn't.

## Запомните
- после do/does/did глагол **have** в начальной форме;
- **don't have to** = не обязательно; **mustn't** = нельзя.

exercises.title: have to, has to или had to

items.text: My sister {{has to}} get up at five every day.
We {{have to}} wear masks in the hospital.
Yesterday I {{had to}} wait for the bus for an hour.
Tom {{has to}} study a lot for his exams.
Last week they {{had to}} move to a new office.
You {{have to}} show your ticket at the gate.

exercises.title: Вопросы и отрицания
exercises.instruction: Вставьте **do / does / did / don't / doesn't / didn't**.

items.text: {{Do}} you have to work on Sundays?
{{Does}} your brother have to wear a suit at work?
I {{don't|do not}} have to get up early tomorrow. It's a holiday.
She {{doesn't|does not}} have to pay. It's free for students.
We {{didn't|did not}} have to wait long. The doctor was free.
Why {{did}} you have to leave the party early?

___ you have to wake up early yesterday?
She ___ have to cook. Her husband cooks.
I ___ to stay at home last night because I was ill.
What time ___ you have to be at work?
They ___ have to pay. It's free.

exercises.instruction: Выберите предложение, которое подходит по смыслу и верно по форме.

items.q: Вы не обязаны приходить (можно прийти, а можно нет).

options: You don't have to park here.
He have to work a lot.
He has to work a lot.
He has to works a lot.

exercises.title: Составьте предложения
exercises.instruction: Составьте предложение или вопрос из слов.

items.prompt: (I / have to / go / to the dentist / tomorrow)

Tomorrow I have to go to the dentist.
Ann has to work on Saturdays.
Do you have to wear a uniform?
Why did she have to leave yesterday?

She doesn't have to cook today.

exercises.title: Напишите о себе
exercises.instruction: Ответьте о себе полными предложениями. Проверьте по образцу.

items.prompt: What time do you have to get up on weekdays?
items.sample: I have to get up at seven o'clock.

items.prompt: Something you have to do every day
items.sample: I have to take the bus to work.

items.prompt: Something you don't have to do at the weekend
items.sample: I don't have to go to work at the weekend.

items.prompt: Something you had to do yesterday
items.sample: I had to buy some food yesterday.

items.prompt: A question to ask a friend about his or her job
items.sample: Do you have to work on Saturdays?
